processing: Little is documented for this garden. Darjeeling black tea is normally made in the orthodox way, withered, rolled, oxidised and fired, more lightly in spring.
harvest_season: As usual in Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush in early summer, then monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, twisted leaf in olive and brown with some pale tips.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold to amber, depending on the flush.
appearance_wet: Soft green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner in later flushes.
taste_profile: Nothing specific to this garden's cup is well recorded. As with other Darjeelings, expect a floral, brisk spring tea and a fruitier summer one.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Use about 85°C for a spring lot.

vintage_note: Usual for Darjeeling: sold by year and flush, with a lot number and leaf grade on single-estate lots. Spring tea is best within about a year. Check the current garden name on any lot, since the similar name Rungeet has been replaced by Kanchaan View.
description:
Rungneet is a tea garden and village in the Darjeeling Pulbazar block, listed alongside gardens such as Singla, Soom and Bloomfield.

Little is written about its processing, so assume the district's orthodox method until a seller tells you more: light oxidation in spring, fuller in summer.

Brew it like other Darjeelings, cooler for first flush and closer to the boil for second, and judge it on the lot in front of you.

The name causes confusion. A garden spelled Rungeet, a short way north of Darjeeling town, was renamed Kanchaan View around 2002; it may be this same garden, but that link is not firmly established.
history:
Little is documented about Rungneet's founding or who planted it. It appears in lists of Darjeeling gardens and in the 2011 census as a village of 1,252 people.

A similarly named estate, Rungeet, took the name Kanchaan View around 2002 and sits at about 3,500 to 4,500 feet with mainly China bushes. Whether the two names refer to one garden remains unconfirmed.
